transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things with my husband’s sister have been going on too long. She’s been working the family business in a way that, to me, looks like she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over like I’m reading too much into it, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been more than a year now.
Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about your sister-in-law’s intentions?

I mean, I guess anybody could say there’s a chance, but I don’t really believe I’m mistaken. This has been going on too long. The way she’s been handling the family business, it really looks to me like she’s trying to get control of the money and keep me out of decisions. People try to make it sound harmless, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
If someone showed you clear proof that your sister-in-law was not trying to take control of the money, would you believe it?

If it was really clear proof, I’d look at it… but honestly, I don’t know that it would change what I know I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for over a year with the family business, and the way she handles things makes it look like she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out. People keep trying to smooth it over, but it doesn’t feel innocent to me.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things, if that’s what you mean. It’s more about what’s happening with the business and how she’s acting.
Do you generally find it hard to trust most people?
I don’t know that I’d say most people. I’m careful with people, sure, but I don’t walk around thinking everybody’s against me. It’s more certain situations where I feel like something isn’t right.
Are you certain that your sister-in-law is trying to take control of the money?

Yes. I mean, I feel certain. I’ve been seeing this for more than a year now with the family business. My husband’s sister keeps working things in a way that puts her closer to the money and leaves me out of decisions. People try to make it sound like it’s nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Aside from your concerns about your sister-in-law, do you currently believe anyone else is deliberately trying to harm, cheat, or undermine you?

No, not really anyone else. It’s mainly my husband’s sister. That’s why I came in—she’s been working things with the family business so she can get closer to the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Have you taken any actions because of this belief about your sister-in-law?

Yes, a little. I’ve skipped some family get-togethers because I just don’t want to be around all that. And I keep certain plans or money matters to myself now, because I don’t want them getting back to my husband’s sister. But other than that, I still do my normal routines and go to church and all that.
Has your sister-in-law actually done anything specific that clearly shows she is trying to take control of the money?

Well, it’s not like she handed me a paper saying it, if that’s what you mean. But I’ve watched how she’s been handling things with the family business for over a year, getting herself closer to the money and leaving me out of decisions. People try to make it sound harmless, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Before this problem with your sister-in-law, did you usually suspect that other people had hidden motives toward you?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal worries about people here and there, but I wasn’t going around suspecting everybody had some hidden plan against me. This thing with my sister-in-law is different.
Has anyone else who has looked closely at the business situation agreed that your sister-in-law is trying to take control of the money?

Not really, no. People keep trying to tell me it’s just business or family stuff, but I know what I’ve been seeing. She’s been working her way closer to the money and leaving me out for more than a year now.
How much has this situation with your sister-in-law affected your day-to-day life?

It’s affected me some. I’ve skipped a few family get-togethers because I don’t want to be around her or have things get back to her. And I keep certain plans or money matters to myself now.

But outside of that, I still do my usual routines. I still go to church and take care of what I need to.
Has this situation been causing you a lot of distress?

I mean, it bothers me, sure. I don’t like feeling like I have to watch what I say or keep things from people. But I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart over it. It’s just… it’s on my mind more than I’d like.
Has your husband ever told you that he also thinks his sister is trying to take control of the money?

No, he hasn’t really said it like that. He tries to smooth it over and make it sound like it’s just family or business stuff. But I know what I’ve been seeing—his sister’s been working her way in closer to the money and pushing me out of decisions for over a year now.
Did this start after a specific change in the family business?
Yes, it was around when the arguments started with my husband’s sister over the family care planning. That’s when I first really noticed it. It’s been going on about a year and two months now.
Do you believe for certain that your sister-in-law is trying to take control of the money, even though no one else agrees with you?

Yes. I do believe it. I know nobody else wants to call it what it is, and they keep saying it’s just business or family stuff, but I’ve watched it happen. She’s been working her way into the family business and the money decisions, and pushing me out for over a year now. So yes, I’m sure about what I’m seeing.
Has anyone directly told you that your sister-in-law is trying to take control of the money?

No, not directly like that. People try to smooth it over or act like it’s just family business, but I know what I’ve been seeing. She’s been working her way into the money decisions and pushing me out for more than a year now.
Has anyone shown you evidence that your sister-in-law is not trying to take control of the money?

No, not really. People just keep telling me I’m making too much of it, or that it’s just family business, but nobody has shown me anything that proves I’m wrong. I know what I’ve been seeing—she’s been working her way into the money decisions and trying to push me out.
Have there been ongoing real arguments or conflicts between you and your husband’s sister about the family business?

Yes, there’s been conflict. I came in because of what’s been going on with my husband’s sister and the family business. She’s been working her way into things so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People try to smooth it over, like it’s nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think it is possible that this is a real family business conflict, rather than your sister-in-law deliberately plotting to take control of the money?

I mean, I guess people can call it a family business conflict, but to me it’s more than that. She’s been working her way into the money decisions and trying to push me out. I’ve been seeing it for over a year, even if everybody wants to smooth it over like it’s nothing.
